readme:
# Kompass Scraper - Global B2B Company Directory

Runs on paid Apify plans. On the FREE plan Kompass refuses the connection and the run stops without charges. The actor needs the proxy access of a paid plan.

Scrape company data from [Kompass.com](https://www.kompass.com), a global B2B directory with 60M+ companies across 70+ countries.

## Plan and connection handling

The actor connects through the proxy access of your Apify plan and switches to a stronger connection level by itself when the site refuses requests. The `unblockMode` input is optional: `auto` (default) switches when needed, `on` starts on the stronger level right away, `off` never uses it and ends the run if the site refuses requests.

If your plan has no proxy access, the run ends with the status "Kompass needs Apify proxy groups not available on your plan (FREE). See README." and nothing is charged. Every run that delivers nothing ends with a reason in the status: `plan_refused` (the plan has no proxy access), `blocked` (the site refused every connection level), `cookie_only` (the site returned pages without company cards) or `parse` (the page layout changed; please report it). Runs that deliver rows end with "N companies delivered."

## Use with AI Agents (MCP)

Connect this actor to any MCP-compatible AI client -- Claude Desktop, Claude.ai, Cursor, VS Code, LangChain, LlamaIndex, or custom agents.

**Apify MCP server URL:**

```
https://mcp.apify.com?tools=santamaria-automations/kompass-scraper
```

**Example prompt once connected:**

> "Use `kompass-scraper` to scrape company data from kompass. Return results as a table."

Clients that support dynamic tool discovery (Claude.ai, VS Code) will receive the full input schema automatically via `add-actor`.

## What data do you get?

For each company, the scraper extracts:

- **Company name** and description
- **Website URL**, phone number, and email
- **Full address** (street, postal code, city, country)
- **GPS coordinates** (latitude/longitude)
- **Employee count** (e.g., "Von 20 bis 49 Mitarbeiter")
- **Year founded**
- **Revenue/turnover**
- **Supplier type** (Exporter, Manufacturer, Service provider, etc.)
- **Product categories** and certifications (ISO, etc.)
- **Company logo**

## How to use

### Option 1: Keywords + country (recommended for programmatic use)

Set `searchQueries` (array of keywords) and `country` (ISO code). The scraper builds the correct subdomain URL for each query.

```json
{
  "searchQueries": ["logistics", "freight forwarding"],
  "country": "PL",
  "maxResults": 40,
  "unblockMode": "auto"
}
```

Each entry in `searchQueries` is scraped independently. Results from all queries are combined up to `maxResults`.

### Option 2: Paste a search URL

1. Go to any Kompass country site (e.g., [de.kompass.com](https://de.kompass.com)) and search for companies
2. Copy the search results URL
3. Paste it into the **Search URLs** field

Works with all Kompass country domains: `de.kompass.com`, `fr.kompass.com`, `gb.kompass.com`, `it.kompass.com`, `es.kompass.com`, and 70+ more.

### Option 3: Paste company profile URLs directly

You can also paste company profile URLs (e.g., `https://in.kompass.com/c/rolex-rings-private-limited/in774979/`) into **Search URLs** to fetch a single company's full profile without paginating. Useful for dedupe workflows: run a search-only pass first, dedupe against your database, then pay for detail only on the new companies.

### Option 4: Paste category URLs (/a/)

Category pages at `/en/a/{slug}/{id}/` list many companies on a single page. A test run on `https://pl.kompass.com/en/a/logistics/25535/` returned 81 companies from one page request.

Find a category URL by browsing Kompass and clicking a category from the left-hand filter panel. The URL in your browser will contain `/a/` followed by a slug and numeric ID.

Example URLs:

```
https://pl.kompass.com/en/a/logistics/25535/
https://de.kompass.com/en/a/logistics/25535/
https://fr.kompass.com/en/a/logistics/25535/
```

Paste them into the **Search URLs** input field. The scraper detects `/a/` paths automatically.

### Country routing

Kompass uses country subdomains, not query parameters. Setting `country: "PL"` routes to `pl.kompass.com`, `country: "FR"` routes to `fr.kompass.com`, and so on. Query parameters like `?country=PL` are ignored by Kompass -- only the subdomain matters.

When `searchUrls` is also set, the `country` field acts as a post-filter that drops SERP results not matching the target country, which helps for long queries that occasionally return off-target companies at the tail.

### Input example (programmatic API call)

```json
{
  "searchQueries": ["logistics"],
  "country": "PL",
  "maxResultsPerQuery": 20,
  "unblockMode": "auto"
}
```

### Input parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `searchQueries` | array | Search keywords. Each becomes one Kompass SERP URL on the correct country subdomain. Primary input for API use. |
| `searchUrls` | array | Kompass search result or company profile URLs, used as-is |
| `searchQuery` | string | Single keyword (legacy, use searchQueries for new integrations) |
| `country` | string | ISO country code (e.g. "PL", "DE", "FR"). Determines subdomain. Required when using searchQueries/searchQuery. |
| `maxResults` | integer | Maximum total companies to scrape (default: 5) |
| `maxResultsPerQuery` | integer | Alias for maxResults. Takes precedence when both are set. |
| `unblockMode` | string | Advanced: `auto` (default), `off`, `on`. `auto` switches to a stronger connection level when the site refuses requests, `on` starts there, `off` never uses it. See "Plan and connection handling" above. |
| `includeDetails` | boolean | Fetch detail pages for full data (default: true) |
| `fetchCatalogueLinks` | boolean | Fetch media page to extract `catalogue_pdf` and `catalogue_video` (default: false) |

## Tips

- **Include Details = ON** gives you email, full address, coordinates, employee count, founding year, VAT/GST number, and more.
- **`catalogue_url`** is always the Kompass media page (listing brochures and videos). Enable **`fetchCatalogueLinks`** to also get `catalogue_pdf` (direct PDF download) and `catalogue_video` (YouTube/Vimeo link) -- this makes one extra request per company.
- **Include Details = OFF** is faster but only returns name, city, phone, website, and categories from search results.
- `unblockMode` can stay `auto`; the actor switches the connection level by itself when the site refuses requests.
- **Category URLs** (`/a/` paths) return more companies per page than search pages. Paste them into **Search URLs**.
- The scraper works with all 70+ Kompass country domains.
- Connections are handled automatically; you do not need to configure anything for a normal run.

## Pricing

Pay per result. The Pricing tab of this Actor lists the events and their prices:

- `directory-start`: charged once per run, after Kompass returned the first page.
- `directory-serp-result`: one per company delivered with search-result data only.
- `directory-detail-result`: one per company delivered with its full profile (charged instead of the search-result event).

Runs that could not reach Kompass are not charged. If the run reaches the maximum charge you set, it stops and the status says how many companies were delivered.


## Notes

- `uk.kompass.com` URLs are automatically mapped to `gb.kompass.com` (Kompass redirects uk to gb) and all URLs are fetched over https.
- Detail rows are billed at the detail price only when the company page yielded data (website, phone, email or address). Otherwise the row falls back to the search-result data and the search-result price.
- On PL pages Kompass shows website, phone and VAT only as a paid option, so those fields are mostly empty there.

## Data protection

This actor returns only data that is publicly visible on the source pages. Results can include personal data, such as names, phone numbers, email addresses and addresses of private persons, sole traders or contact persons. Where the source labels an entry type, it is included so you can filter the results yourself.

You are responsible for using the data lawfully, including the GDPR/DSGVO, national data-protection laws and unfair-competition rules (e.g. UWG) for marketing and outreach.
